swahili.stressRule: Rule: stress almost always falls on the second-to-last syllable.

origins.safari: Arabic safar (“journey”) — and from East Africa a loanword to the world
origins.simba: simply means “lion” — The Lion King’s hero bears his species name
origins.rafiki: “friend” — also the wise ape in The Lion King
origins.hakuna-matata: literally “there are no worries” — real Kiswahili, not just a movie quote
origins.polisi: English police — loanwords get a final vowel in Kiswahili
origins.chai: like German “Chai” — via Persian and Arabic from Chinese
origins.kahawa: Arabic qahwa — the same word became “coffee”
origins.shule: from German! “Schule” entered Kiswahili in colonial times
origins.hela: from the German “Heller” coin — small change became the word for money
origins.kiswahili: the language’s own name — ki- is the noun-class prefix for languages
origins.kilimanjaro: Africa’s highest mountain — stressed, as almost always, on the second-to-last syllable

dialogGloss.mambo: Mambo? — Poa! (“What’s up?” — “Cool!”): casual, among friends
dialogGloss.hujambo: Hujambo? — Sijambo! (“Are you well?” — “I’m fine!”): the neutral standard greeting
dialogGloss.habari: Habari yako? — Nzuri sana! (“What’s your news?” — “Very good!”)
dialogGloss.asante: Asante sana! — Karibu! (“Thank you!” — “You’re welcome!”, literally “welcome”)
dialogGloss.shikamoo: Shikamoo! — Marahaba. The respect greeting for elders; only the elder replies Marahaba.
